scope: Separate Windows host backing bound and Docker guest capacity for runtime preparation and setup readiness
supersedes: artifacts/cloud005/consumer-verification.json preparation coverage; the earlier API worker-admission/HTTP projection results remain separate evidence
contract: Windows host bound and Docker guest filesystem are checked independently against40GiB before publishing a new runtime job and again immediately before Docker build.
Guest evidence requires current engine identity, fresh execution observation, fresh measured available bytes; nil/stale/zero/under-budget observations refuse.
An absent sandbox image does not block storage measurement or the explicitly authorized cold build.
An installed image removes the cold-build demand from readiness but still requires fresh confirmed host and guest observations.
New work is blocked under uncertain storage; existing builds and worker leases are retained.
Non-required Linux setup behavior stays unchanged; cloud backing setup owns its own prerequisites.
limitations: 40GiB is an explicit conservative prerequisite (32GiB build working allowance plus8GiB reserve), not a measured peak or lifetime quota.
No Docker build/allocation or native Windows VHD probe was performed in this test.
Native Windows runtime acceptance and the subsequent shared-observation-cache change require their own verification.
